data.title: Venture Global CEO sees final investment decisions on two key projects in next year's H1
data.description:
Venture Global's  growth plans have progressed well, and the company intends to make final investment decisions for the expansion of its CP2 and Plaquemines projects in next year's H1, and some equipment orders have already been placed, CEO Michael Sabel told The Wall Street Journal in an interview Wednesday.

Venture Global is advancing the two expansion projects to push its liquefied natural gas production capacity past 100M metric tons/year before the end of 2030.

The expansion at CP2 is expected to provide an additional 10M tons/year of LNG, and the Plaquemines expansion should increase production by 7M-8M tons/year.

LNG suppliers and analysts are split between those that forecast an impending supply glut once energy markets stabilize and those that expect demand will continue to rise, but Sabel told WSJ that the company does not believe there is a supply glut.

Instead, Venture Global expects a small LNG shortage heading into the early 2030s with large supply projects likely to run behind schedule, Sabel said.

The outlook is also clouded by questions over when lost volumes from Qatar will return to the market, as damage to the country's facilities from the Middle East conflict has cut the country’s export capacity by ~17%.

data.title: Anthropic Prices IPO at $83 a Share on Strong Demand — WSJ
data.description:
By Corrie Driebusch and Kate Clark

Anthropic sold more shares than it planned at a higher price than expected for its initial public offering, after investors requested several times more shares than the artificial-intelligence giant was selling.

The company behind the Claude chatbot sold shares at $83 each, which was above the price range it had guided, according to people familiar with the matter.

On a fully diluted basis, the offering is expected to value the company at around $1.5 trillion. The shares are expected to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT" midday Thursday.

The company had been aiming to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 apiece. It was planning to raise another $26 billion from a group of big investors including Amazon.com, Nvidia and Google in a private-placement share sale.

Anthropic received strong demand from investors spanning mutual funds, hedge funds, venture-capital firms and individuals, even as its roadshow pitch came during a bout of volatility in AI-linked stocks. It was also interrupted by the dramatic departure of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO.

Prospective investors typically request far more shares of IPOs than they expect or even want in the offering. Some investors spent Wednesday worrying that they might end up getting nothing or very small allocations even after submitting jumbo requests.

Updates to follow as news develops.

Write to Corrie Driebusch at corrie.driebusch@wsj.com and Kate Clark at kate.clark@wsj.com

data.title: This ₹1,200 crore fund manager has an advice for Vedanta Aluminium - Here's what he said
data.description:
Sanjay Parekh, Founder & CIO of Sohum Asset Managers, believes the management of Vedanta Aluminium should initiate a meaningful share buyback, calling the stock an "amazingly deep value" play.

According to Parekh, the company's strong cash flow allows it to reward shareholders via both buybacks and dividends while still becoming completely debt-free within the next two to three years.

He went on to explain the valuation math during an interaction with CNBC-TV18 on Wednesday, November 18:

Parekh mentioned that Vedanta Aluminium currently has a market capitalization of ₹1.43 lakh crore. Against that, the business has a debt of ₹20,000 crore for the current year. He went on to add that even after funding capital expenditure and paying dividends, the company is paring down debt at a rate of ₹2,500 crore to ₹3,000 crore per quarter.

Assuming that the London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium prices sit at $2,800 per tonne, Parekh estimates Vedanta Aluminium to generate an attributable Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation of ₹33,000 crore to ₹34,000 crore on 2.5 million tonnes of production. This is aided by value-added products and the expiration of previous loss-making hedges.

Trading at just under five times its projected EBITDA on conservative LME assumptions, the stock offers a compelling risk-reward ratio. While Parekh noted that predicting whether LME prices will swing toward $2,500 or $3,000 is difficult, his demand-supply analysis indicates prices are unlikely to see a sharp downturn.

The business boasts a Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of over 50%, with Return on Equity (ROE) expected to climb even higher. Having already paid a dividend of ₹8 per share, Parekh sees scope for payouts to rise as high as ₹20 per share alongside a potential share repurchase program.

"This is a time when the management should meaningfully do a buyback, and they can pay dividends, buy back, and yet in two three years the debt will be free, it will be debt free, it’s that compelling," Parekh added.

Shares of Vedanta Aluminium ended 5.8% lower on Wednesday at ₹374. The stock demerged from the Vedanta Ltd. business and listed as an independent entity on June 15 this year. The stock is down 28% from its listing price of ₹522.

data.title: Battery Mineral Resources Announces Appointment of Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Battery Mineral Resources Corp. (OTCQB: BTRMF) ("Battery" or "BMR" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Frikkie Kruger as Chief Financial Officer of the Company, effective December 1, 2026.

Mr. Kruger, based in Massachusetts, is a Chartered Accountant (South Africa) and a member of the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants with 20 years of progressive finance leadership in the mining and resources sector, with a particular focus on copper. He has held senior finance roles in South Africa, Zambia, the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Middle East, South America and the United Kingdom, working with companies listed on the London, Johannesburg and Santiago stock exchanges.

Mr. Kruger was most recently Group Financial Manager at Moxico Resources PLC, which operates the Mimbula copper mine on the Zambian Copperbelt. He previously served as Chief Financial Officer of Bayete Energy Resources and as Senior Financial Reporting Manager at Enaex Africa. He has supported mining businesses through both the development and operating stages and has built finance functions from start-up. His expertise includes IFRS and U.S. GAAP reporting, multi-entity consolidation, multi-currency treasury, C1-C3 and all-in sustaining cost (AISC) modelling, payable metal calculations and SOX-aligned internal controls.

Laz Nikeas, Chief Executive of BMR, stated, "We are very pleased to welcome Frikkie to the Company. His copper-focused finance and public market experience will be a strong addition to our team."

Mr. Kruger added, "I am delighted to join Battery Mineral Resources at such an important stage for the Company and the Punitaqui Mining Complex. I look forward to working with Laz, the Board and the broader team to strengthen BMR's financial foundation, reinforce disciplined capital management and support the Company's growth strategy."

The Company also announces that it has granted 500,000 restricted share units ("RSUs") to Mr. Kruger pursuant to the Company's restricted share unit plan (the "Plan"). The RSUs will vest in three equal annual instalments commencing on the first anniversary of the date of grant and are subject to the terms and conditions of the Plan and the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange.

About Battery Mineral Resources Corp.

Battery Mineral Resources operates the Punitaqui Mining Complex, a historic copper, gold, and silver-producing mine in the Coquimbo region of Chile. The Company's portfolio also includes 100%-owned ESI Energy Services Inc. and North American mineral exploration assets. The Company is focused on providing shareholders with accretive exposure to copper and the global trend of electrification while targeting growth through cash flow, exploration and acquisitions in favorable mining jurisdictions. Further information about BMR and its projects can be found on www.bmrcorp.com.

data.title: Regeneron Says Muscular Disorder Treatment Livsayis Gets FDA Approval
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals said the Food and Drug Administration has approved Livsayis as a treatment for certain adult patients suffering from generalized myasthenia gravis.

The condition is an autoimmune muscular disorder which can result in weakened muscles, trouble breathing, and altered vision, among other symptoms. The Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America said a 2021 study estimated that 37 out of every 100,000 people in the U.S. have myasthenia gravis.

Livsayis, or cemdisiran, is a small interfering RNA therapeutic that reduces levels of circulating C5 protein, limiting terminal complement activation, a key driver of the disease, the company said. Regeneron added Livsayis is its first approved siRNA therapy and neurology medicine.

Livsayis is the first and only approved siRNA therapy in generalized myasthenia gravis and the only FDA-approved treatment for the condition administered subcutaneously four times a year, according to Regeneron.

Write to Stephen Nakrosis at stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com

data.title: Dow Jones falls another 550 points, nears 'technical correction' - Here's what transpired
data.description:
Benchmark indices on Wall Street had a mixed session on Wednesday, November 18, as the post-Nvidia earnings optimism fizzled out and traders digested the Fed minutes, Anthropic's IPO pricing, and a meltdown in metal prices globally.

The Dow Jones fell 550 points on Wednesday, taking the three-day loss for the index past 2,100 points. The 30-stock index had declined 750 points on Monday and another 850 points on Tuesday as well. Pressuring the index was UnitedHealth, one of its biggest weightage constituents, which fell 10%, along with shares of Chevron and Caterpillar, which fell between 2% to 4%.

With this fall, the Dow Jones is just 900 points away from a 10% fall from its peak, which would drag the index into a "technical correction."

The S&P 500 ended 0.2% lower, extending its losing streak for the fifth straight session, while both the Nasdaq indices - Composite and 100, gained 0.4% each, putting an end to their recent losing run for now. The losses seen in Nvidia were offset by its peer companies, AMD, Broadcom and Amazon, each of which saw their stock price surge between 4% to 5%, lending support to the tech-heavy index.

More Rate Hikes Coming?

Traders also analyzed the Fed minutes, where most officials agreed that more rate hikes are warranted in the future to bring inflation down to their 2% target. Two officials also suggested a 50 basis points rate hike in the December policy if the inflation data turns out to be unfavourable.

Earlier in the day, Fed Governor Christopher Waller hinted at a similar policy stance in an interview to CNBC, suggesting that people will need to be "shocked" if inflation pressures keep persisting.

"I’m very, very concerned about inflation. It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out. If you really want to get it down, you’ve got to start taking more aggressive actions. You might need to like, shock people."

Metals Meltdown Continues

Metals continued to sell-off in the global markets overnight, with Gold prices falling another 3.5% to their lowest level since September 2025, while Silver prices fell over 5%. Silver prices had made a record high of over $120 earlier this year, but have now corrected to less than $45 an ounce. The sell-off in Copper prices also continued with the metal falling to the lowest level since April on the London Metals Exchange (LME).

An aggressive policy posture from the Fed, which in-turn strengthened the US Dollar, is adding to the pressure on Metal prices. The US Dollar Index is now nearing levels of 104.

All Eyes On Anthropic Listing

AI Lab Anthropic will be making its Wall Street debut later this evening in what promises to be the world's biggest IPO in history, surpassing the SpaceX issue just a few months earlier.

Reports suggest that the company has priced its IPO at $83 per share, which is above the earlier marketed range of $70 to $78 apiece. In case Anthropic does sell all 825 million shares as intended, it will raise $68.5 billion through the IPO, and along with the pre-committed investment of $26 billion, the total fund raise would cross $90 billion.

Both Amazon and Google, which own significant stakes in the company, are likely to see their holdings be valued at over $100 billion each.

data.title: Yorkton Equity Group Inc. Announces Financial Results for the Third Quarter Ended September 30, 2026
data.description:
Edmonton, Alberta--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Yorkton Equity Group Inc. ("Yorkton" or the "Company") announces its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

"The Company continues to focus on growing and strengthening its Alberta operations," said Ben Lui, President and Chief Executive Officer. "The acquisition of The Crystallina Residence earlier this year expanded our residential rental portfolio in Edmonton, while the recent acquisition of Lui International Group Inc., which provides property management services for our Alberta properties, represents an important step toward vertically integrating our operations. We believe Alberta provides greater opportunities to leverage our operational expertise and generate long-term value for shareholders. Our ongoing efforts to sell the British Columbia investment properties will allow us to better focus our attention and resources on Alberta, while also generating proceeds to help address the Company's upcoming convertible debenture maturities in early 2027."

Q3 2026 Financial Highlights

Yorkton's strategy is to focus on expanding its portfolio in Alberta, where the Company believes it can more effectively leverage its operational expertise. Consistent with this strategy, and in consideration of upcoming convertible debenture maturities in early 2027, the Company is pursuing the sale of its investment properties in British Columbia.

As at September 30, 2026, six British Columbia investment properties, comprising 128 residential rental units, were classified as held for sale, with an aggregate fair value of $25.64 million. Related liabilities included $0.13 million of refundable security deposits and $9.30 million of mortgages payable. The Crystallina Residence is a 184-unit multi-family residential complex constructed in 2016, comprising three condominium-quality buildings and a free standing amenity building in Edmonton, Alberta.

Discontinued Operations

The net loss from discontinued operations for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $592,924 and $4,781,816, respectively, compared to net income of $653,694 and $824,247 in the comparative periods in 2025.

The change in results was primarily attributable to fair value decreases of $740,851 and $5,653,128 in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to fair value increases of $500,000 in the comparative periods in 2025. The fair value decreases in 2026 were primarily driven by changes in market capitalization rates.

Overall Financial Results

Yorkton reported a net loss and comprehensive loss of $700,675 and $5,108,573 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to net income and comprehensive income of $62,900 and $980,869 in the same periods in 2025.

The change in overall financial results was primarily attributable to fair value decreases of $740,851 and $5,653,128 in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to fair value increases of $100,000 and $1,424,577 in the comparative periods in 2025. The fair value decreases in 2026 were primarily driven by changes in market capitalization rates.

Commercial rental revenue and net operating income from the Company's Alberta commercial property and British Columbia commercial unit were not significant during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

About Yorkton

Yorkton Equity Group Inc. is a growth-oriented real estate investment company committed to providing shareholders with growing assets through accretive acquisitions, organic growth, and the active management of multi-family rental properties with significant upside potential. Our current geographical focus is in Alberta, supported by a diversified and growing economy and strong population in-migration. Our business objectives are to achieve growing Net Operating Income ("NOI") and asset values in our multi-family rental property portfolio in strategic markets across Western Canada.

The management team at Yorkton Equity Group Inc. has well over 35 years of prior real estate experience in acquiring and managing rental assets.
